newsitem.title: CHINA: Pegasus places convertible pref shares.
newsitem.headline: Pegasus places convertible pref shares.

text.p: Pegasus International Holdings Ltd said on Monday it had placed convertible preference shares to Citicorp Everbright China Fund (CECF) for a total consideration of US$15 million.
The shares carry a coupon of 4.25 percent and carry the right to convert to ordinary shares of the sport shoe maker within four years at a price of HK$1.7272 per share.
Upon conversion, Pegasus would issue the equivalent of 8.5 percent of its enlarged share capital.
Pegasus said the funds raised would be used to finance additional production lines at the group's facilities in China.
"This investment will enable us to expand our customer base," said Pegasus chairman Thomas Wu.
Over the next three years, Pegasus said it will set up an additional 16 producyion lines, facilities for the manufacture of ethylene-vinylacetate and polyurathane midsoles, rubber outsoles and molds.
CECF is a fund organised by Citicorp in 1995. Other investors include China Everbright International Trust and Investment Corp and a unit of the Brunei Investment Agency.
It has total funds of US$177 million, of which 50 percent is already invested in 12 manufacturing projects in China.
"The challenge is to find good partners and good investments," said Vincent Fan, chief executive of Citicorp Capital Asia Ltd. "There is no shortage of liquidity."
